questions.q: What does the Decision element do, in Salesforce's own words?
options: Evaluate a set of conditions and route the flow through the outcome that matches — the equivalent of an if-then statement
Permanently delete records that no longer meet a condition
Pause the flow until a human approves it
Combine two collections into one without any conditions
questions.explain: Decision performs the equivalent of an if-then statement, routing the flow based on which outcome's conditions are met.

questions.q: A Decision element (Define Manually) has outcomes A, B, and C in that order, plus a Default. A record matches both A's and B's conditions. Which path runs?
options: Both A and B run, one after another
B's path, because it's more specific
A's path — the first outcome in the list whose conditions are true, and nothing after it is evaluated
The Default Outcome, since two outcomes matched
questions.explain: With Define Manually, outcomes are evaluated top to bottom; the first match wins and later outcomes (even if also true) are never evaluated.

questions.q: When does the Default Outcome's path run?
options: Every time the flow runs, in parallel with other outcomes
Only when none of the other outcomes' conditions are met
Only when the flow is a record-triggered flow
Only when explicitly called from another flow
questions.explain: The Default Outcome has no conditions of its own and runs only when every other outcome evaluated false.

questions.q: What's different about Flow Builder's newer Define with AI (Advanced) decision method, compared to Define Manually?
options: It requires a Loop element to work at all
It only works in Marketing Cloud flows
Its outcomes are evaluated simultaneously via written instructions, so outcome order doesn't affect which one wins
It removes the need for a Default Outcome entirely
questions.explain: AI Decision outcomes are evaluated all at once from plain-language instructions, unlike Define Manually's strict top-to-bottom order.

questions.q: In the Check Case Details example from this lesson, what does the Severity 0 outcome's condition check?
options: Whether the record was created more than 30 days ago
Whether the triggering case's Case Type equals Downtime
Whether the case Status equals Closed
Whether the Account has more than 10 open cases
questions.explain: The Severity 0 outcome's visible condition is Triggering Case > Case Type Equals Downtime.
